> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #376 implements issue #29 by letting the `/answer` route handle mentions from PR review bodies more usefully.
- It passes `REQUEST_SOURCE_KIND`, `REQUEST_COMMENT_ID`, and `REQUEST_COMMENT_URL` into the answer prompt.
- It updates the answer prompt with a narrow `pull_request_review` exception so the agent can inspect review comments and post targeted inline replies when requested.
- It adds focused tests for the prompt content, workflow env wiring, and supplemental prompt variable allowlist.

## Review
The implementation matches the requested prompt-driven direction, and the PR check is passing. However, the current prompt change has a few minor unresolved risks around normal `/answer` prompt noise, inline-reply reruns, and the workflow’s always-posted final body. Reviewer outputs disagreed on severity: one review said SHIP, while the Claude and rubrics reviews flagged minor prompt/docs follow-up.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Review-specific prompt context is not conditional | WARNING | The prompt now shows review trigger metadata for every `/answer` route, and a current human inline comment asks to keep that conditional. |
| Inline reply path needs final-body and rerun guards | WARNING | The prompt permits inline replies but does not require a non-empty final answer body or tell the agent to avoid duplicate same-agent inline replies on reruns. |
| Usage docs are not updated | WARNING | The answer route docs still describe only a normal inline workflow response and do not mention the new review-triggered inline reply behavior. |

## Progress
- The PR already wires the needed trigger metadata into `agent-router.yml` and covers that wiring in tests.
- The existing `run.ts` supplemental prompt allowlist already includes the three `REQUEST_*` vars, so no `run.ts` change is required for the current design.
- The human conditionality concern is already present in an inline thread on `agent-answer.md:7`; I did not duplicate it.
- Posted one new inline comment on `agent-answer.md:15` for the non-empty final body issue.
- No review threads were resolved or minimized.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Review-specific prompt context is not conditional</summary>

**Cause:** [`agent-answer.md` lines 7-10](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/c8eb149bea9cecc7491fdc89cfcbba332de6970b/.github/prompts/agent-answer.md#L7-L10) render review metadata unconditionally, even for normal `/answer` runs.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a computed supplemental prompt variable such as `ANSWER_REVIEW_CONTEXT`, populate it only when `source_kind == pull_request_review`, allowlist it in `run.ts`, and render that block instead of always rendering the metadata.

**Comments:** This is grounded in the current human inline review thread, which says normal answer routes do not need this block.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Inline reply path needs final-body and rerun guards</summary>

**Cause:** [`agent-answer.md` line 15](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/c8eb149bea9cecc7491fdc89cfcbba332de6970b/.github/prompts/agent-answer.md#L15) allows targeted inline replies, but [`post-response.ts` lines 42-43](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/c8eb149bea9cecc7491fdc89cfcbba332de6970b/.agent/src/cli/post-response.ts#L42-L43) still posts a fallback error if the final answer body is empty.

**Candidate solutions:** Tell the agent to always return a non-empty final response when it posts inline, even if only a short summary. Also add prompt guidance to inspect existing thread replies and skip duplicate Sepo-authored inline replies on reruns.

**Comments:** Claude flagged the empty-body path; the rubrics review flagged idempotency. These are overlapping prompt-safety concerns.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Usage docs are not updated</summary>

**Cause:** [`agent-actions.md` line 9](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/c8eb149bea9cecc7491fdc89cfcbba332de6970b/.agent/docs/usage/agent-actions.md#L9) still describes `answer` only as an inline response through `agent-router.yml`.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a short note that `pull_request_review`-triggered `/answer` runs receive review metadata and may inspect related inline comments for targeted replies.

**Comments:** This is not a runtime blocker, but it is a docs-sync gap for a behavior change.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: the remaining issues are concrete prompt/docs edits and are safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
MINOR_ISSUES

## Action Items
- [ ] Make review-specific `/answer` metadata and instructions conditional so normal answer prompts do not show review-only context.
- [ ] Add prompt guidance requiring a non-empty final body when posting inline and avoiding duplicate Sepo-authored inline replies on reruns.
- [ ] Update the answer route usage docs for the new `pull_request_review` inline-reply behavior.

## Summary of PR/Issue

## Review
The implementation is close and the overall design matches the requested prompt/context-driven approach. Reviewers mostly agree the prior fix-pr pass resolved the earlier gaps, but the current Codex review correctly flags one remaining prompt contradiction that can weaken the PR’s core behavior.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Base answer prompt contradicts review inline-reply exception | WARNING | `.github/prompts/agent-answer.md` still says not to post comments directly via `gh` after the conditional review context says targeted inline replies are allowed. |
| Optional empty review id guard is missing | INFO | `buildAnswerReviewContext` assumes `pull_request_review` always has a review id; malformed trigger metadata could render incomplete `gh api .../reviews/` examples. |

## Progress
- Current head `7b0ef38d229636d5a8ca0f149f6e2704974207bf` makes review context conditional through `ANSWER_REVIEW_CONTEXT`.
- Current docs now describe review-triggered `/answer` inline replies, non-empty final bodies, and duplicate-skip behavior.
- Current tests cover prompt rendering, workflow metadata, context generation, and docs.
- Posted one new inline comment on `.github/prompts/agent-answer.md:11` for the unresolved prompt contradiction.
- Resolved same-agent thread `PRRT_kwDOSOhEMM6F6KYe` because the non-empty final-body concern is fixed.
- Left the older human-authored conditionality thread unresolved per the same-agent thread cleanup guard.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Base answer prompt contradicts review inline-reply exception</summary>

**Cause:** The rendered review prompt includes `ANSWER_REVIEW_CONTEXT`, which says `pull_request_review` answers may post targeted inline replies, but the later base instruction at [`agent-answer.md#L11`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/7b0ef38d229636d5a8ca0f149f6e2704974207bf/.github/prompts/agent-answer.md#L11) still bans direct `gh` comments unconditionally.

**Candidate solutions:** Scope line 11 to normal `/answer` runs, or phrase it as `Except for the review-triggered exception above, ...`.

**Comments:** Codex flagged this as the remaining issue; Claude and rubrics otherwise considered the latest head acceptable.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Optional empty review id guard is missing</summary>

**Cause:** [`buildAnswerReviewContext`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/7b0ef38d229636d5a8ca0f149f6e2704974207bf/.agent/src/answer-review-context.ts#L11) returns review context whenever `sourceKind` is `pull_request_review`, even if `commentId` trims to an empty string.

**Candidate solutions:** Add an early `if (!commentId) return "";` after trimming the review id.

**Comments:** This is defensive only; current portal metadata should provide a review id for real `pull_request_review` triggers, so it should not drive automation by itself.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: one concrete prompt wording change is needed so the review-triggered inline-reply exception is not contradicted by the base answer instructions.

## Final Verdict
MINOR_ISSUES

## Action Items
- [ ] Update the base `/answer` no-GitHub-write instruction so it explicitly excludes the review-triggered inline-reply exception.

Yes, that is a real issue.

For resumed `/answer`, the agent may not receive the full `agent-answer.md` route prompt again. It can receive the lightweight continuation prompt from `buildContinuationPrompt()` instead. So if the review-specific behavior only lives near the top of `.github/prompts/agent-answer.md`, an existing PR answer session can miss it.

I’d handle it in two layers:

1. Keep the route prompt clean and conditional for fresh sessions.
2. Put the review-triggered context into the continuation prompt too, because that is the prompt actually sent on resumed sessions.

So the durable fix should be in `.agent/src/prompt-continuation.ts`, not only `.github/prompts/agent-answer.md`.

Something like:

- Always include the latest request text in the continuation prompt.
- Include trigger metadata only when present.
- If `REQUEST_SOURCE_KIND=pull_request_review`, append a small review-specific block telling the resumed agent to fetch the review and related inline comments before answering/posting.
- If we later build a computed `ANSWER_REVIEW_CONTEXT`, use the same computed text in both the full answer prompt and the continuation prompt so the two paths cannot drift.

Yes, exactly.

If the first `/answer` run for that PR is triggered from a PR review, there is no resumed session yet, so ACPX receives the full initial `agent-answer.md` prompt. In that cold-start path, the review-specific context has to be present in the initial prompt.

The nuance is: it should be **conditional initial context**, not unconditional metadata for every answer route.

So the shape should be:

- Fresh session: full `agent-answer.md` includes `${ANSWER_REVIEW_CONTEXT}` near the task setup, and that variable is non-empty only for `pull_request_review`.
- Resumed session: full prompt is skipped, so `buildContinuationPrompt()` also includes the same `${ANSWER_REVIEW_CONTEXT}` when the latest trigger is `pull_request_review`.
- Normal `/answer`: `${ANSWER_REVIEW_CONTEXT}` is empty, so no extra review guidance appears.

That gives the review-triggered cold-start run the needed instructions without duplicating them in resumed runs.
